chapter: Big bands, Depression work and the WPA band
title: The Cotton Club on the Airline Highway
summary: The club, formerly the Rio Rita, had Joe Phillip and Mike DeLay on trumpet. Ernie and Dejan describe its location and food.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then they have a club out on the airline highway, they call it Cotton Club now. They used to be named. The Rio Rita. The Rio Rita. The Rio Rita. And they wanted to rename the club, so they asked somebody to name the club. And how they rename it up until they did. They still call it Cotton Club. Yeah, still call it Cotton Club. Big club on the airline highway. We used to work there. Yeah. And matter of fact, Mike DeLay was his trumpet player. No, we know how to call him Mike DeLay. Joe Phillip.
Joe Phillip started that with me. Joe Phillip, front of Santiago. Then he left then Mike DeLay.
Yeah. Mike used to play trumpet and Lawrence DeRooks, our Larry band would play piano. When Larry had a job to play, he would put Mike on piano and hire me to play trumpet. Yeah, he played trumpet.
Cotton Club, I'll never forget that.
How far out is that about? I can't remember.

Not too far. You know where the Claiborne Bridge is? Yeah. You know where you cross over Claiborne? Well, there's about three blocks on this side. Three or four blocks. You used to have a big rodeo every Sunday, right opposite there. A big, a big lot, big rodeo. Oh, man. It'll be fine. Remember the cook at night, asking what y'all to eat tomorrow night. Tell them what you want to eat. Yeah. Anything. Always leave that with a bag of shrimps or- Crab. Crab.
